name: sbml-annotation-tagging
title: SBML MIRIAM-Annotation Organ Tagging (Planned)
question:
Can parsing curated SBML MIRIAM annotations (Uberon/taxon/GO terms embedded
as RDF in each BioModels entry) lift organ-tag recall past the current
name-only synonym-match ceiling (~20% on the 25-result glucose-regulation
query, 7.5% at full-corpus scale), while preserving the precision the
existing matcher already demonstrates?

study_card.goal: For each BioModels entry, parse embedded MIRIAM RDF annotations for Uberon/taxon/GO terms and cross them against the HRA reference-organ Uberon set, comparing tagged-model count and per-organ precision against the current name-only synonym match.
study_card.mechanism: Planned: an SBML/MIRIAM-annotation reader (parse <bqbiol:is>/<bqbiol:isVersionOf> RDF triples from each model's XML) feeding the same organ_to_models index shape glucose-biomodel-do already produces, run alongside the existing synonym matcher for a side-by-side recall/precision comparison.
study_card.expected_result: A materially higher tagged-model fraction than the current 20% (25-result query) / 7.5% (full corpus) name-only ceiling, without degrading the precision glucose-biomodel-do already demonstrated (organ assignments concentrating correctly on pancreas/liver for glucose-regulation models).
study_card.main_expert_question: Is annotation-based tagging precise enough (curated models are not guaranteed to carry complete or correct MIRIAM annotations) to fully replace name-only synonym matching, or should the two be combined (union of hits, annotation-first)?
study_card.future_work: The real MIRIAM-annotation parser/composite is not yet implemented. This scaffold's baseline placeholder reuses the existing glucose-biomodel-do composite (name-only synonym matching) purely so the study resolves and renders; the annotation-based tagging mechanism itself is future work.

biological_summary:
glucose-biomodel-do demonstrated that scanning only a BioModels entry's
*name* for HRA reference-organ synonyms is precise (it correctly
concentrated glucose-regulation hits on pancreas and liver, the two
organs glucose-homeostasis biology predicts) but recall-limited: 80% of
the 25-result query and 92.5% of the full 1,096-model curated corpus went
untagged. Curated BioModels entries, however, frequently carry embedded
MIRIAM (Minimum Information Requested In the Annotation of Models) RDF
annotations that cross-reference standard ontologies — Uberon (anatomy),
NCBI Taxonomy (species), and GO (biological process/function) — directly
on model or species elements. Parsing those structured annotations,
rather than pattern-matching free-text titles, is a natural next lever to
raise recall: an entry whose name never says "pancreas" may still declare
a Uberon pancreas term on one of its species or compartments.
limitations: TBD — planned study, not yet implemented.

remaining_uncertainties: Is name-only synonym matching precise enough to trust for downstream multiscale coupling, or does it need SBML MIRIAM-annotation-based tagging to raise recall?
